newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Taiwan bourse seen aided by Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Taiwan bourse seen aided by Hong Kong.

text.p: Taiwan's TAIEX bourse index is expected to post a comfortable increase on current levels by the end of the year, but the speed of the rally should cool after the middle of the year, according to analysts in a Reuters survey of world stock index forecasts.
Eleven analysts in the survey predicted a mean level of 8,520 by end-1997, compared with the close of 8,255.07 on March 12.
The average forecast is more optimistic than the 7,925 given in a similar survey three months ago.

The index is expected to take a more bullish mood during 1998, according to the survey, with a mean forecast from 10 analysts of 10,750, around a 30 percent increase on current levels but still well off the all-time high of 12,495.34 recorded in February 1990.
LEONARD HSEUH, HEAD OF RESEARCH, NIKKO SECURITIES:
Most expect China to try to keep a bullish Hong Kong economy from July. Taiwan shares will follow suit, rising with Hong Kong's expected celebration rally.
But that rally should cool off in August because of an unfolding power struggle in China.
ALEX CHIU, FUND MANAGER, CAPITAL SECURITIES:
A correction for the overheated market is expected, but the long-term bullish trend hasn't changed. The index will continue to rise as the economy is seen continuing to recover in 1998.
